02-094.r: Civilizations north to south → Aztec (northern Mesoamerica) → Maya (southern Mesoamerica) → Muisca → Inca.
02-094.h: Going down the Americas: A-M-M-I (Aztec, Maya, Muisca, Inca).

02-095.r: World's oldest civilization (book) → Mesopotamian (present-day Iraq); Egyptian (Nile) civilization emerged after it.

02-096.r: First proper system of writing → Sumerian civilization; its cuneiform script is one of the earliest writing systems.

03-001.r: 'Arya' in classical Sanskrit → 'noble man'. 'Aryan' denotes a speech (language) group, not a race; book prints 'a superior race', against its own explanation.
03-001.c: Book prints (d) 'a superior race', but its own explanation says the Aryan idea was not racial. 'Aryan' denotes a speech (language) group, so (c) is the correct answer.

03-003.r: Oldest and most important Veda → Rigveda (four Vedas: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, Atharvaveda).

03-005.r: 'Trayi' (Vedatrayi) → the three Vedas: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda.
03-005.t: Atharvaveda is not part of the Trayi.

03-006.r: 'Varna' first in the Rigveda (Purusha Sukta): Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra born from mouth, arms, thighs, feet of Purusha.

03-008.r: Atharvaveda → medicine; Rigveda → God grace (prayers); Yajurveda → sacrifice process; Samaveda → music.

03-009.r: Rigveda → hymns and prayers; Yajurveda → hymns and rituals; Samaveda → musical hymns; Atharvaveda → charms and spells.

03-010.r: Magical charms and spells → Atharvaveda (earliest description).

03-011.c: No answer printed; 1028 is the hymn count while mantras are 10552, so no option fits 'mantras' exactly.

03-012.r: Rigveda → collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns (each about ten verses); one of the four Vedas (Shruti).

03-013.r: Brahmanas: Rigveda → Aitareya; Samaveda → Panchvisha; Atharvaveda → Gopatha; Yajurveda → Shatpatha and Taittiriya.

03-016.r: Gopatha Brahmana → the only Brahmana of the Atharvaveda (Shaunaka and Paippalada recensions).

03-017.r: Samhita of Shukla Yajurveda → Vajasaneyi (option 'Vajasanami'); Shukla Yajurveda is only verse, Krishna Yajurveda has verse and prose.

03-018.r: Ninth Mandala of Rigveda (114 hymns) → wholly devoted to Soma; Rigveda has 10 Mandalas.

03-020.r: Rites of Yajnas → Yajurveda ('wisdom of sacrificial formulas'): prose and verse formulae for priests; compiled a century or two after Rigveda.

03-021.r: Veda with Krishna and Shukla branches → Yajurveda; Krishna has irregular, mixed mantras, Shukla a systematic order.

03-022.r: Samaveda → compiled from the Rigveda; shortest Veda, verses for chanting; 1875 verses, all but 75 or 99 taken from Rigveda.

03-023.r: Earliest evidence of iron use in India → Atranjikhera (on Kali river, Ganga tributary); identified by Cunningham, excavated by R.C. Gaur.

03-024.r: Iron in the Indian subcontinent began about 3000 years ago (Iron Age about 1000 B.C.; smelting 1300-1200 B.C.) → none of the above.

03-025.r: Upanishads → philosophy; 'Upanishad' = pupils sitting near the teacher to learn the secret doctrine.

03-027.r: Salvation (Moksha) → first discussed in the Upanishads, not in the Vedas; the core self is the Atman (soul).

03-028.r: Nachiketa–Yama (lord of death) dialogue → Kathopanishad (Katha Upanishad); Nachiketa was a 12-year-old boy.

03-030.r: Upanishadic king Asvapati → Kekaya (on Beas). Other philosopher-kings: Janak (Videha), Pravahan Jabali (Panchala), Ajatshatru (Kashi).

03-031.r: Vedic literature order → Samhitas → Brahmanas → Aranyakas → Upanishads; first two = Karma Kanda, last two = Gyan Kanda.

03-032.r: River mentioned most in early Vedic literature → Sindhu (called 'Hiranyayi'); most sacred river → Saraswati ('Naditama').
03-032.t: Most mentioned = Sindhu; most pious = Saraswati.

03-034.r: Rigvedic rivers of Afghanistan → Kubha (Kabul), Krumu (Kurram), Gomati (Gomal), Suvastu (Swat); show Aryan links with Afghanistan.

03-036.r: Kubha → Kabul; Parushni → Ravi; Sadaneera → Gandak; Shutudri → Sutlej.

03-037.r: Mahanadi in the Mahabharata → Chitrotpala (so 'none of these'); 'Chitrotpala Ganga' in Someshwar Dev's Mahoba copper plate.

03-038.r: Mahanadi's mythological name: Vayu Purana → Nilotpala; Matsya Purana → Chitrotpala.
03-038.t: Vayu Purana = Nilotpala; Matsya Purana and Mahabharata = Chitrotpala.

03-039.r: Later (post-) Vedic customs → four Purusharthas (Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha) and four Ashramas (Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sanyasa).

03-040.r: Pancha Mahayajnas (Brahma, Deva, Pitra, Bhuta, Atithi Yajna) → duty of the Grihastha Ashram (householder), the foundation of society.

03-041.r: Vedic Rita → fundamental moral law of the universe (impersonal); Dharma → duties to oneself and others. Both statements correct.

03-042.r: 'Rita' → natural law (universal natural order), of Vedic origin; upheld by Varuna, hence called 'Ritasyagopa'.
03-042.h: Varuna guards Rita: Ritasyagopa = protector of Rita.

03-043.r: Priest of the Vedic gods → Brihaspati (Deva-guru, teacher of the gods).

03-044.r: Brahmavadini who composed Rigvedic hymns → Lopamudra (wife of Agastya); others: Vishwawara, Sikta, Nivavari, Ghosa.

03-045.r: Nishka → Rigvedic gold neck ornament ('Nishka-Griva'); later the word meant a gold coin.

03-048.r: Boghaz-Koi inscription (Asia Minor, Turkiye) → names four Vedic gods: Indra, Varuna, Mitra, Nasatya; linked with Aryan movement from Iran to India.

03-050.r: Boghaz-Koi → 14th century B.C. inscription naming Vedic gods Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatya.

03-051.r: Original Aryan homeland → Bal Gangadhar Tilak, 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas' (North Pole/Arctic); theory not accepted by historians.

03-052.r: 'Purusha Medha' → Shatpatha Brahmana (Shukla Yajurveda) and Taittiriya Brahmana (Krishna Yajurveda); historians mostly discuss it with Shatpatha Brahmana.
03-052.c: No answer printed; the book says three of the options fit.

03-053.r: Shatpatha Brahmana: King Videgha Madhava (Videha) with his priest Rishi Gautama Rahugana carried the sacred fire eastward.

03-054.r: Axis of Aryan culture in the post-Vedic period → Kuru-Panchala region (advances in science, astronomy, religion, philosophy).

03-055.r: 'Gotra' first occurs in the Rigveda, meaning 'cow shelter' or 'herd of cows'; meaning 'family lineage' came later (post-Vedic).

03-056.r: Early Vedic religion → worship of nature (fire, water, wind) and yajnas.

03-057.r: Rigvedic religion → mainly sacrifice (Yajna) and rituals; domestic sacrifice was the rule; gods were pleased by Yajna.

03-058.r: Battle of Ten Kings (Dasharajnya, Rigveda) → on the bank of Parushni; Bharata king Sudas defeated a confederacy of ten kings.

03-061.r: Panchajana (five Rigvedic tribes) → Yadu, Turvasu, Druhyu, Anu, Puru; Kikat was not among them.

03-062.r: Book: chief livelihood of the ancient Aryans → agriculture (along with hunting).

03-064.r: Vrihi → rice; Mudga → mung bean; Yava → millet (per this list); Ikshu → sugarcane.
03-064.t: Yava usually means barley; this list had no barley, so Yava → millet.

03-066.r: Vedic system of governance → hereditary (descended) monarchy; a few examples of election by the people.

03-067.r: Vedic Sabha → assembly of the learned and elite (book's answer: council of ministers); Samiti → assembly of common people; both checked the king.

03-068.r: Sabha and Samiti called 'two daughters of Prajapati' → Atharvaveda.

03-069.r: Sabha and Samiti as separate institutions → Atharvaveda; Rigveda (tenth Mandala) also mentions both, roles not clearly separated.

03-070.r: Rigvedic assembly with judicial function → Sabha (mentioned eight times in Rigveda); other assemblies: Samiti, Vidatha.

03-071.h: Bhaga = share: Bhagadugha collects the king's share.
